chunks: And by his chain, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) judged regarding a slave who was co-owned between two men: one of them emancipated his share while the slave was young, and the other retained his share until the one who had freed his half grew up. He said: He shall be appraised at the value on the day the first (owner) freed his share, and the freed slave is ordered to work to earn his other half that has not yet been freed, until he pays it off.

key_terms.حرَّر: Emancipated/freed — the act of granting legal freedom
key_terms.قضى: Judged/ruled — used for authoritative judicial decisions by the Imam
key_terms.نصيب: Share/portion — the co-owner's undivided interest in the slave
key_terms.يسعى: Works/strives — the legal obligation to earn money to buy his freedom
key_terms.يقضيه: Fulfils/pays off — the discharge of the slave's financial obligation
key_terms.يقوَّم: Is appraised/valued — the judicial assessment of the slave's monetary worth

ai.seo_question: What was Imam Ali's ruling on a jointly owned slave whose share was partially emancipated?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a legal ruling of Imam Ali (AS) on the case of a jointly owned slave where one co-owner emancipates his portion while the slave is still a minor. Imam al-Baqir (AS) narrates that Imam Ali ruled the slave's value must be fixed at the date of the first emancipation, and the partially freed slave is legally obligated to work to purchase his remaining half from the other co-owner. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of fixing compensation at the time of the original legal act, protecting both parties from market fluctuations.
